River #otters 🦦 are making an awesome comeback around North America’s #GreatLakes 🌊 after nearly disappearing by the 1970s. Thanks to reintroduction programs, cleaner water, and restored wetlands 🌱, breeding populations are now growing again in places like #Ohio, #NewYork, and #Ontario 🗺️.
Good news! River otters are coming back across the Great Lakes region. www.rewildingmag.com/the-river-ot...

By the 1970s, pollution, trapping, habitat loss had driven river otters out of the Great Lakes. By the 1990s, efforts in the US and Canada to restore damaged habitat and reduce toxic discharges were successful, and rivers were again healthy enough to support an apex predator like the river otter.

River Otter surfaces while foraging for crustaceans near the mouth of the Black River into Lake Superior on the UP of Michigan. Otters are smart and extremely playful water dependent creatures that manage to survive in areas where most surface water is frozen. #Mammals #otters #riverotter #otter

River otters have staged a remarkable comeback across North America’s Great Lakes after disappearing from many waterways by the 1970s. Reintroductions beginning in the 1980s, combined with wetland restoration and pollution controls under the 1972 US–Canada Great Lakes Water Quality Agreement […]

River otters are back in the Great Lakes! 🦦 40 years ago, they were locally extinct in 11 states. Thanks to decades of conservation work, they've reclaimed their home across the region. Cleaner water, healthier ecosystems, and otters playing again where they belong. That's a win worth celebrating.

Captain Bartholomew Fredrick once held the world record for sailing 4 large otters strapped together around lake Ontario for 6 days straight. Others have tried to beat the record only for 2 to be hospitalized and 1 to die while trying to strap the otters together

River otters are making a big comeback in the Great Lakes region after being nearly wiped out by hunting and pollution. Thanks to decades of restoration and cleaner water, these playful predators are thriving again in Ohio, Michigan, New York, and Ontario.
